title: Metallic Bonding and Properties of Metallic Solids
notes: **Electron sea model:** metal atoms release valence electrons into a common pool. The positive metal ions are held together by the electrostatic attraction to this sea of delocalized electrons.

**Properties explained:** high electrical and thermal conductivity (delocalized electrons move freely), malleability and ductility (layers of ions can slide without breaking bonds because electrons readjust), luster (free electrons absorb and re-emit light).

**Alloys:** mixtures of metals. Substitutional alloys (Cu-Ni, similar atomic sizes) and interstitial alloys (steel: C atoms in Fe interstices). Alloys are usually harder and have lower conductivity than pure metals.
**Bond strength:** metallic bond strength depends on the number of delocalized electrons per atom and the charge on the ions. Transition metals are strong because they have more valence electrons.
**Mercury exception:** Hg has a weak metallic bond because its 6s electrons are relativistically contracted and less available for bonding, making it liquid at room temperature.
